defects.summary: The `foreign` reclassification withholds the `untracked` FINDING in exactly the record-loss state that the `untracked` text itself names as one of its four causes, and the note then asserts the opposite — "So no bundle here delivered it".
defects.evidence: check_provenance.py:878 gates only on `not in_lock`, never on what the record could have known. Constructed and run against the branch (fixture under tmp_path, ephemeral surface): store holds hook-installed `alpha` plus `helper/` whose SKILL.md declares `name: some-other-name`; record is PRESENT and names only `alpha` — the state `render` describes as "present and empty … it rewrote the record after failing to READ one, which forgets everything from before", and which the untracked finding lists verbatim as cause three. Result: `provenance: 2 on disk, 1 hook-installed, 0 unattributed, 1 foreign … 0 findings`, exit 0. On main the same fixture yields `[untracked] helper` and exit 1. The note that replaces it states "So no bundle here delivered it" — a claim the tool cannot support in that state, since the forgotten-record cause is precisely "a bundle delivered it and the record no longer says so". A federated registry that does not run agentskills' `name-dir-mismatch` lint supplies the mismatched frontmatter; the fix report's stillOpen claims "the install record already answers that case first", which is only true while the record still holds the entry. Nothing in the diff tests this state.

defects.summary: `foreign_notes` is emitted store-wide with no lock gate, so a directory the lock names gets both `hand-placed-over-locked` ("it will not survive the next session start") and a `[foreign]` note ("the hook will never remove it") in one report.
defects.evidence: check_provenance.py:1685 passes the whole `foreign` dict to `foreign_notes`, while classify (:878) gates the ROW on `not in_lock`. The classify docstring claims "`hand-placed-over-locked` keeps priority over the label" — true of the column only. Ran the diff's own fixture shape with the lock naming it (`seeded_skill(store, "alpha", "something-else")` + `write_lock(..., "alpha")`, ephemeral): output carries FINDINGS (1) `[hand-placed-over-locked] alpha` … "it will not survive the next session start, which replaces the directory with the registry's copy" AND NOTES (1) `[foreign] alpha` … "So no bundle here delivered it … the hook will never remove it, because the hook removes only what its record proves it installed". The headline also disagrees with itself: `_tally` prints "0 hook-installed, 1 unattributed" with no foreign column, next to a foreign note. The diff's `test_a_name_disagreement_the_lock_declares_is_still_a_finding` asserts the finding and the row but never that the note is absent, so nothing catches it.

defects.summary: `shadow-copies-differ` reddens a healthy pair: the comparison digests the full personal tree, but the account copy is by construction the uploader's FILTERED zip, so any `__pycache__`/`.pyc`/`.b64` artefact in the personal copy is read as divergent instructions.
defects.evidence: `plugins/adam-local/skills/sync-skills/sync_skills.py:523` defines `_SKIP_DIRS = {__pycache__, .pytest_cache, .git, .venv, node_modules}` and `_SKIP_EXTS = {.pyc, .pyo, .b64}`; `skill_payload()` (:767) deliberately reads members back out of the real ZIP "so the exclusion rules in ``_include_in_zip`` can never drift out of sync" — i.e. `--verify` already solves exactly this and the new code re-introduces it. Ran on the branch: `shadowed_store(tmp_path)` (the diff's own healthy fixture) plus `writing-adrs/__pycache__/helper.cpython-311.pyc` → `FINDINGS (2)` with `[shadow-copies-differ] writing-adrs`, exit 1, on two copies whose SKILL.md bytes are identical. This is the exact failure mode the change's own rationale forbids ("a doctor that reddens the ordinary case is one whose findings get skipped"), and it is reachable: the checkout already carries four `__pycache__` dirs under `plugins/`, and `_walk_up`'s docstring blesses running this suite from the installed copy at `~/.claude/skills/skills-doctor/scripts`. It also falsifies the comment at check_provenance.py:266, "the two delivery channels disagree about line endings and, so far, about nothing else" — a claim a reader can check against `_include_in_zip` and find wrong.

defects.summary: A personal directory that is not a skill at all (no SKILL.md) is reported as a two-channel collision, and — being unavoidably different from the real account skill — as a `shadow-copies-differ` FINDING at exit 1.
defects.evidence: check_provenance.py:1155 intersects `names` (from `scan`, which returns EVERY non-dot directory regardless of SKILL.md) with `account` (from `skill_names`, which requires SKILL.md). Ran on the branch: store holds hook-installed `alpha`, an empty leftover `beta/`, and `synced/beta/` holding a real skill. Output: `[shadow-copies-differ] beta … delivered by BOTH channels under one bare name`, exit 1. Nothing is delivered under `beta` by the personal store — the session listing sees one copy, from one channel — so both the collision claim and the divergence finding are false. The diff's negative control `test_a_name_only_one_channel_delivers_is_not_a_shadow` covers only the case where the personal store has no directory of that name at all, so it does not reach this.

defects.summary: The benign shadow note asserts the DIRECTION of the line-ending difference ("the account store is CRLF where the registry is LF") without measuring it; the code only knows that folding CRLF reconciled the pair.
defects.evidence:
check_provenance.py:1210 sets that sentence on the `norm_mine == norm_theirs` branch unconditionally. Ran on the branch with the direction reversed — personal copy written as `b"---
name: alpha
---
body
"`, account copy LF (`account_copy(..., crlf=False)`) — and the report still prints "byte-identical once CRLF line endings are folded to LF — the account store is CRLF where the registry is LF". Same defect class as the `_cause` rule the file elsewhere enforces: a reader who checks the bytes finds the sentence wrong. Both digests are already in hand, so the direction is measurable rather than assumable.

defects.summary: New comments carry unasserted counts and "Measured:" claims about code that is not in the tree — the #120 defect class the branch was meant to avoid.
defects.evidence: test_check_provenance.py:2719 "(Measured: multiplying `shadow_noted` by the lock count changes the output not at all.)" and :2746 "(Measured: it did.)" both describe experiments on mutated source that no longer exists anywhere a reader can reach; neither is reproducible from the checkout. check_provenance.py:768 "Measured on two independent hosted cloud sessions (#123)" and test_check_provenance.py:2319 "The exact shape measured in two independent hosted cloud sessions" carry a count ("two") that nothing asserts — the premise these support IS assertable (I confirmed on this hosted machine that `~/.claude/skills/session-start-hook/SKILL.md` declares `name: startup-hook-skill`), but the session count is not. Separately, check_provenance.py:274 argues the near-copy was chosen over a flag because "a parameter that can change what it hashes is a way for the copy to drift while the binding still passes" — yet `test_the_digest_matches_the_generators` binds only `digest_skill_dir`, so the copy it chose instead has no binding at all; the sentence also calls that function "one of three hand-written copies" immediately above a fourth hand-written implementation of the same manifest algorithm in the same file.
